questions.question: Ron suggests that in his presentation he should have

analyses.content: 录音中明确提到，Ron认为自己本该在演讲中讲清楚是美国人首创（pioneered）了JIT这个理念。
你可能听到supermarket或Japan就想选B或C，但录音里明确说这些是后来受启发的，不是他认为自己遗漏的重点。

But actually, one thing I should have made clearer and talked about was the fact that the Americans actually pioneered the idea of just-in-time, though it wasn't called that. Henry Ford and his cars, in fact, at the turn of the 20th century. And later, a big US supermarket chain used it, and this was where Toyota in Japan got the idea for its car making.

questions.question: The tutor says that in his presentation Ron omitted

analyses.content: 导师直接指出Ron在演讲中没有给JIT下一个清晰的定义（clearly defined）。
虽然录音中提到了“classic business theory”和“aim”，但这些是Ron已经讲过的内容，并非他遗漏（omitted）的部分。

Uh, now, before we go any further, I think I would suggest that you should have stopped and clearly defined just-in-time for your seminar colleagues. You said its aim was to reduce waste, and you mentioned that classic business theory assumes that stock or inventory of parts are counted as assets, but just-in-time sees them as unnecessary waste. But you never told us that JIT simply means waiting until the last moment to order new supplies as you need them.

questions.question: The tutor suggests that in the service sector, JIT is

analyses.content: 导师解释JIT在服务业不太适用，因为服务业卖的东西是看不见且无法计数的（can't actually see or count）。
录音提到JIT目前很流行（fashionable），直接排除了B选项，同时完全没有提及重要客户是否接受。

And while you're at it, you might want to find out about cases where JIT might not be suitable, and that's in service industries like tourism or healthcare, where customers are paying for something that they can't actually see or count. Although JIT is fashionable today, some people would say it hasn't proved so successful in the service sector as it has with the manufacturing of goods that can be quantified.

analyses.content: Ron自己承认讲话忽快忽慢，导师也表示赞同，这完全对应“不规律（irregular）”。
这里的忽快忽慢不要和“太突然（sudden）”混淆，它强调的是整体节奏的不稳定。
I sometimes seemed to talk fast and sometimes slow. I was on edge, I guess. Yes, you were.
导师明确批评Ron的演讲目的不够具体（not very specific）、太宽泛（general），对应选项中的“太模糊（vague）”。
听到“not very specific”和“general”就能直接对应vague，不要过度脑补其他毫不相关的形容词。
And as well as that, your purpose wasn't very specific. In future, you need to lay out exactly what you're going to cover and why. Make it clear and concise and not so general.
导师评价Ron在段落过渡时太生硬（abrupt），完美对应“太突然（sudden）”。
这里的“quickly”指的是切换的突兀感，而不是说话语速，不要选错。
And what about my transitions from one section to the next? Well, you didn't link the sections, did you? You went too quickly from one to the next. It was all just too abrupt.
导师指出PPT上的图片虽然好看，但跟演讲内容没太大关系（didn't have much to do with），对应“关联性太弱（loosely related）”。
录音夸了图片“lovely”，所以绝对不是批评图片本身不好看或太死板。
Now, your PowerPoint visuals were lovely, but sometimes I got the feeling that, nice as they were as pictures, they didn't have much to do with what you were talking about, right?
导师提醒Ron听众是外行，需要简化词汇，说明他原本的用词太专业了（technical）。
听众听不懂是因为词汇过于专业，而不是因为不够正式（informal）。

And you know, another thing, I could see from the other students' reactions, they just didn't understand some of the vocabulary I was using. Mm, good point. Well, remember, your audience were laymen, mostly without knowledge of JIT. So you need to simplify and try to put things in everyday English.
导师指出Ron站得笔直且缺乏动作，让人觉得他对这个话题不够感兴趣（not very interested），对应“缺乏热情（unenthusiastic）”。
虽然录音里有“stood straight”，但这里强调的是缺乏活力和兴趣，不要误以为是在批评他太过于死板或可预测（predictable）。
And lastly, I'll just mention your body language. You didn't use gestures, and you just stood straight without any animation. It didn't make you seem very interested in the subject.
